data.title: Why Rivers Overflow
data.passage: Heavy rain falls on high mountain peaks during the spring months. Melting snow rushes down the rocky hillsides too quickly. However, a wide river channel can hold the extra water safely. Similarly, thick grass and tall trees slow down the flowing streams. To fix this overflow hazard, workers build high concrete walls along the banks. As a result, nearby towns stay dry and safe from damage.
